overall: The AG found the former chair individually violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a committee quorum and serially relaying opinions, but not intentionally; the committee as a whole was not found in violation. Compliance and public release of the emails were ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged a quorum of the committee deliberated by email outside an open meeting, starting with a Dec 2, 2011 email from the chair copied to members.
allegations.key_passage: Here, Chair Loomis' communications violated the Open Meeting Law's express prohibition on communication to a quorum about matters within the body's jurisdiction outside of a meeting.

allegations.summary: A Jan 25, 2012 email from the chair sent a budget-question document containing his opinions to a quorum of members.
allegations.key_passage: This email therefore constituted an impermissible deliberation outside of a meeting.

allegations.summary: An April 23, 2012 email from the chair to non-members asked that his budget opinions be forwarded to the other two members, allegedly creating a serial quorum communication.
allegations.key_passage: This communication violated the Open Meeting Law because, by requesting that his opinions be forwarded to the other Committee members, the Chair was attempting to facilitate communication between and among a quorum of the Committee on public business within the Committee's jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Whether the committee as a whole, not just the chair, violated the law through the chair's emails, given members' lack of responses.
allegations.key_passage: Because no other dialogue or exchange of opinions resulted between or among a quorum of the Committee, the Committee as a whole did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law ordered.
Public disclosure of the nine emails discussed in the letter at the committee's next meeting, subject to permitted redactions or withholding.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Furthermore, we order the Committee to publicly disclose the nine emails discussed in this letter at the Committee's next meeting.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
